transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you here today?

Yeah, um, thanks for seeing me. I guess... I came in because I just, I can’t stop thinking about my face. Specifically the left side of my face, it just looks completely off. Like, my nose and my jaw are totally crooked. 

I really started fixating on it when I saw my college ID photo, and then with some of my classes being online, you have to have the camera on, right? So I'm just sitting there staring at my own video feed for hours, and it’s so obvious how lopsided everything is on the left side. I can't even pay attention to the lectures. And it's driving me crazy because when I bring it up to my family or friends, people always say they don’t see it. They act like I'm making it up or seeing things, but it's right there. How could they not see it? 

It's gotten so bad that it's messing up my job, too. I work as a CNC tool operator and programmer, and lately, I can barely even focus on my tool paths or the machines. I just feel like everyone in the CNC lab is staring at my face and noticing how messed up my jaw is before they even notice my work. If I'm setting up a mill and a coworker walks by, I just know they're looking at my crooked nose. I try to turn my head so they only see my right side, but I can't work like that all the time. It's just this constant, heavy feeling all day, every day, and I just can't turn it off. I don't know how to make it stop.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy, especially around the time you started noticing these concerns about your face?

I mean... I wouldn't really say I feel hopeless? Or like I've lost interest in stuff. It's not like that at all. Like, I still *want* to do things. I still really enjoy working on my own machining projects in my garage, or, you know, playing games online with my friends. I actually just spent like three weeks designing and cutting this custom aluminum keyboard case from scratch, which was awesome, so the interest is definitely still there. 

It's just... it's not that I don't care about things, it's that I literally can't stop thinking about my jaw long enough to actually enjoy them the way I used to, you know? Like, I'll be right in the middle of a game, or trying to dial in the tolerances on my mini-mill, which I normally love doing, and then I'll just sort of feel how lopsided my face is. Or I'll catch my reflection in the monitor screen when it goes dark for a second during a loading screen. And boom, that's it, that's all I can think about for the rest of the night. I'll just sit there touching the left side of my face trying to figure out how to hide it.

So I'm not sitting around crying or feeling down like I have no energy or whatever. I have energy. It's just all being completely sucked into worrying about how crooked my nose is. It's way more like this constant, buzzing stress in the back of my head than feeling depressed. Because my mom actually asked me the exact same thing last week, she was like, "Are you depressed?" and I had to explain to her for like an hour that it's not depression, it's just this massive, glaring problem with my face that I can't escape. If my face was normal, I'd be completely fine and doing all my normal stuff.
Do you find yourself doing certain things over and over again, like checking your reflection, touching your face, or trying to cover it up, because of how you feel about the left side of your face?

Oh, man. Yeah. All the time. It's... honestly, it's pretty much taking over my mornings, to the point where it's a huge problem. Like, before I leave for school, I just get completely stuck. I'll go into the bathroom to get ready, and the lighting in there is just super harsh, you know? It's those awful overhead vanity bulbs. So I'll catch the left side of my jaw in the mirror, and I just lean in, and I end up standing there for... I don't even know, maybe forty-five minutes? An hour? Just turning my head back and forth, checking the angle, touching my jawline to see if I can push it back into place. 

And then I don't even trust the mirror because mirrors flip your face, right? So I pull out my phone camera and switch it to the front-facing lens, and I take like twenty pictures from different distances and different lighting just to see how crooked it actually looks to other people in the real world. I'll zoom in on my nose, then my jaw, over and over.

Then I try to fix it, or at least hide it. I'll spend forever messing with my hair, trying to get the front to sweep over the left side of my face just right to kind of balance out the lopsidedness. Or I'll start changing my shirts. I have these different collared shirts and hoodies, and I'll put one on, but then I'll look in the mirror and think the neckline draws way too much attention to my crooked nose. So I take it off, put another one on, check the mirror again, check the phone camera again... I'll literally go through five or six shirts, just making a huge pile on my floor, trying to find the one that hides the angle of my jaw the best. 

And then, I always end up going downstairs and asking my mom. I'll corner her in the kitchen and be like, "Mom, does my jaw look swollen today? Is the left side super obvious?" And she always gives me the same tired look and says it looks completely normal, but I just don't believe her. So I end up asking her like three or four more times before I even make it out the door, just begging her to tell me if it looks weird. 

By the time I actually leave... well, if I even leave. Sometimes I do this whole routine for so long that I completely miss my morning lab. I'll just look at the clock and realize I'm an hour and a half late for my CNC class, and there's no point in going. And even if I do force myself out the door and make it to campus, I'm just so mentally wiped out from the whole ordeal. I show up to the shop and I'm just completely exhausted. I can't even focus on writing my code or setting up the tooling because I spent all my energy just trying to get out of my own bathroom.

Have you noticed any other kinds of thoughts or worries that pop into your mind that you don't want there—like upsetting ideas, images, or urges that bother you and won't go away, even if they're not about your face?

Um, no... no, not really. I mean, I don't think so? When you say upsetting ideas or urges, like, if you mean stuff outside of how I look, then definitely not. I honestly don't even think I have the mental capacity to worry about anything else right now. It’s like my brain’s hard drive is just completely full, you know? There's zero free space for other random worries to even pop up. 

Like, I don't worry about leaving the door unlocked or, I don't know, germs, or having weird random images flashing in my head or anything like that. It's just... it always, always comes back to my jaw and my nose. I could be doing something totally normal and unrelated. Like, the other day I was writing up this complex G-code sequence for a 5-axis mill we have at the shop, which takes a ton of concentration. Because if you mess up the Z-axis clearance by even a fraction of an inch, you're going to crash the spindle right into the vise and cause thousands of dollars in damage, not to mention getting chewed out by the floor manager. So I'm sitting there, totally focused on the math, and I don't have any random upsetting thoughts about the machine, or hurting someone, or whatever else people worry about. I just... I'll just suddenly feel the asymmetry in my face again. It's like, boom, the code is gone, and all I can think about is how my jaw is sitting wrong. 

So, yeah, it's never anything else. I almost wish my brain would get stuck on something else for once, just for a change of pace, you know? Like, let me worry about my car's transmission for a day instead. But no, it's a hundred percent just this constant, endless loop about how lopsided my left side is. There's just literally no room in my head for any other kind of unwanted thought.
How much do these concerns about the left side of your face interfere with your ability to function in your daily life, like in school, at work, or with friends?

Honestly, it’s… it’s messing up pretty much everything right now. Like I was saying before about the mornings, I get so stuck in the bathroom that I just don't go. And it’s gotten to the point where I’ve missed multiple CNC labs, which is bad enough, but I’m also missing my actual shop shifts. Like, I just literally cannot get myself out the door. I’ll be standing there, obsessing over the angle of my jaw, and the time just ticks by until it’s way too late to even show up. 

And the thing is, my faculty mentor—he's the guy who oversees the whole machining program and helps us get these industry placements, which are super competitive—he actually pulled me aside the other day. He was super serious about it, too. He told me that because of my attendance and missing those shop shifts, my work placement could actually be in jeopardy. Which is huge, you know? That placement is basically my whole career path. It’s the whole reason I'm in the program, and I might lose it entirely just because I can't let people see my face. But I just can't force myself to go when I look like this. 

And it’s not even just work and school, either. It’s my whole life outside of that. I completely stopped playing soccer. I used to play in this intramural league every Sunday, which I honestly loved, but I just… I can’t do it anymore. When you’re running around on the field, everyone is looking at you, and you get sweaty, and your hair gets messed up, so I can't even use my hair to hide the left side of my face like I normally try to do. So I just quit. I told the guys I pulled a hamstring or something, but the real reason is I just don't want people looking at me. 

Same thing with volunteering. I used to volunteer on Saturday mornings, but I dropped out of that, too. I just couldn't handle the thought of standing there, interacting with all these strangers, knowing they were probably staring right at my crooked nose and my lopsided jaw while I talked to them. It’s just too exhausting to constantly wonder what they're thinking about my face. So I just stay home now. I just want to stay in my room or my garage where nobody can look at me. So, yeah, it’s basically dictating every single part of my day.
